visualReview.notes: Inspected all 11 current portable frames including the compact preview. The individual rectangular compound has an open paved courtyard and axial gate, pointed arcades on pale round columns with simplified capitals, muted red/cream arch wedges, a polygonal fountain canopy, cap-roof rows and a taller middle entrance bay. The prayer hall has a stepped central dome with four lower cap masses and corner domes, opaque arched windows, and two double-balcony minarets with pointed grey tips. Refined round supports and placed arch borders outside the actual wall faces before final captures. Roof partitions, facade rhythm and all heights remain picture estimates. Fine carving, calligraphy, fountain fixtures and unseen interiors are omitted.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected all 11 final shared/geographic-flat views, including the north-up map overlay. Six existing shared 256² limestone, marble, continuous sandstone, standing-seam metal, cast bronze and wood graphs serve seven merged roles. Shared low-frequency textures use metric UVs and linear palette tints; opaque panes are blue-grey. Zero embedded images, unique facade atlases or copied ornament. The muted red/cream arch borders are original polygonal abstractions. Every graph is read once; eviction leaves zero live model geometries. Placement follows the raw compound and open-court rings. Flat placement proves transforms and replacement, not precise terrain contact.

fidelityReview.notes: Individual medium-fi Fatih Istanbul Mosque: central stepped dome composition, two double-balcony minarets, pale masonry hall with recessed windows, open courtyard arcades with muted red/cream arch wedges, grey cap roof rows, entry gate and polygonal fountain canopy. Coarse mapped compound and roof controls retained; detailed partitions and all heights estimated from two pictures. Six existing shared 256² graphs, seven merged roles and four budgeted LODs. Fine art, furnishings, adjacent monuments and unseen interiors omitted. No retained or current map height tags are available. All vertical dimensions are explicit picture estimates: main hall eaves 16 m, cross-dome supports 22 m, central drum 26–31 m, central cap 31–41 m plus 1.5 m finial; two minaret tips 64 m with balcony bands near 40 and 49 m. Courtyard eaves 9 m, lower cap domes to 11.5 m, central hall-entry roof to 17 m; fountain canopy to 8 m. These are visualization dimensions, not surveyed facts. Minor caps, stairs, arch depths, facade rhythm and unseen faces are original medium-fi approximations. Only two useful actually inspected pictures and normal viewer PMTiles/DEM were used. The circular current roof part guides one lower roof mass but supplies no independent height or precise architectural identity. No survey claim, copied artwork, redistributed photographs or furnished interiors. The surrounding medreses, tombs and gardens remain separate host content.
